title: तीन घुम्ती उपन्यासमा लैङ्गिक उत्पीडन र प्रतिरोधी चेतना {Sexual Harassment and Resistance Consciousness In the Tinghumti Novel}
nepali: उपन्यासकार विश्वेश्वरप्रसाद कोइरालाको तीन घुम्ती उपन्यासले इन्द्रमायाका माध्यमबाट नेपाली समाजमाविद्यमान पितृसत्ताको उत्पीडन तथा विभेदलाई अभिव्यक्त गरेको छ । नेपाली समाजको विकासमा युगौंदेखि सामन्तवादी संस्कारको प्रभाव रहेको देखिन्छ । सामन्ती समाजको परिवारमा सामन्तवादको प्रभाव रहेको देखिन्छ । नेपाली समाजमा पुरुषको शासकीय वर्चस्व रहेको पाइन्छ । सामन्ती समाजमा परिवारभित्र बाबुको भूमिका रहेको देखिन्छ । नेपाली समाजमा पनि परिवारभित्र बाबुको भूमिका प्रमुख रहेको पाइन्छ । छोराहरूलाई बाबुको सम्पतिको हकदार मानिने कुरा वर्तमानमा पनि कायम रहेको देखिन्छ । समाजमा महिलाको भूमिका स्वतन्त्र रहेको देखिँदैन, किनभने नारीको विवाह नहुँदासम्म उसले बाबुको रेखदेखमा चल्नुपर्ने हुन्छ त्यस्तै विवाहपछि पतिका आदेशमा चल्नुपर्ने हुन्छ भने बुढ्यौलीमा छोराको अधिनमा जीवन चलाउनुपर्ने भएकाले उनीहरू जन्मदेखि मृत्यु नहुँदासम्म पुरुषकै बन्धनमा रहेको देखिन्छ । नारीलाई स्वतन्त्रता चाँहिदैन भन्ने नेपालीसमाजको क्रियाकलाप विपरीत इन्द्रमायाले जन्म घरमा बाबुको आज्ञा अवज्ञा गरी पर्वते बाहुन केटालाई आफैपति वरण गर्नु, विवाह घरमा पतिसँग मात्र सहवास गरेर बच्चा जन्माउनुपर्ने सामाजिक परम्परा विपरीत अन्य पुरुषबाट गर्भधारण गरेर छोरी जन्माउनु, पति र छोरी मध्ये एकलाई रोज्नुपर्दा मातृत्वलाई महतव दिएर पतिको सहाराविना पनि नारीहरूले जीवन चलाउन सक्छन् भन्ने प्रतिरोधी चेतना प्रस्तुत गरेकी छ । उसको पितृसत्ताविरुद्धको विद्रोहले सचेत नारीहरु लैङ्गिक विभेदका लागि सङ्र्ष गरेर आफ्नो स्वपन कायम राख्न सक्षम रहेको देखिन्छ । {Novelist Bishweshwar Prasad Koirala's Tinghumti novel has expressed the oppression and discrimination of patriarchy in Nepali society through Indramaya. Feudal culture seems to have influenced the development of Nepali society for ages. Feudalism seems to have an influence on the family of feudal society. In Nepali society, male domination is found. In feudal society, the role of father seems to be within the family. In Nepali society too, the role of father is found to be prominent in the family. The fact that sons are considered to be entitled to father's property seems to be maintained even today. The role of women in the society does not seem to be independent, because a woman has to be under the care of her father till she gets married. Contrary to the Nepali society's practice that women do not want freedom, Indramaya disobeys her father's orders at home and chooses a mountain Brahmin boy as her own husband. It has presented a resistance consciousness that women can lead a life even without the support of their husbands. Her revolt against patriarchy seems to have enabled conscious women to maintain their dream by fighting for gender discrimination.}
american_english: Through Indramaya, the novelist Bishweshwar Prasad Koirala's novel Teen Ghumti expresses the oppression and discrimination of patriarchy existing in Nepali society. Feudal culture appears to have held sway over the development of Nepali society for ages. The influence of feudalism appears to be present in the family of feudal society. In Nepali society, men are found to hold the reins of power. In feudal society, the role of the father within the family appears to be present. In Nepali society too, the role of the father within the family is found to be the prominent one. The notion that sons are considered entitled to the father's property appears to remain in place even today. The role of women in society does not appear to be independent, because until a woman is married she must live under her father's care; likewise, after marriage she must live under her husband's orders, and in old age she must live under her son's authority — for these reasons, they appear to remain bound to men from birth until death. Against the practices of Nepali society that women do not need freedom, Indramaya, defying her father's command in her birth home, chooses a Parbate Brahmin boy as her own husband; contrary to the social tradition that in the marital home she must bear children only through intercourse with her husband, she conceives from another man and gives birth to a daughter; and when forced to choose between her husband and her daughter, giving priority to motherhood, she presents a resistant consciousness that women can lead a life even without their husband's support. Her revolt against patriarchy shows that conscious women, struggling against gender discrimination, are able to hold on to their dreams.
british_english: Through the figure of Indramaya, the novelist Bishweshwar Prasad Koirala's Teen Ghumti gives voice to the oppression and discrimination of patriarchy as it exists within Nepali society. Feudal culture appears to have influenced the development of Nepali society for centuries. Within the family of feudal society, the influence of feudalism is apparent. In Nepali society, the dominant hand of the male is found to prevail. In feudal society, the father's role within the family is apparent. In Nepali society, too, the father's role within the family is found to be the prominent one. The convention that sons are deemed entitled to their father's property appears to remain in force even today. Women's role in society does not appear to be independent, for until a woman is married she must live under her father's care; after marriage, she must live under her husband's commands; and in old age, she must live under her son's authority — owing to which they appear to remain shackled to men from birth until death. Contrary to the practices of Nepali society which hold that women do not desire freedom, Indramaya, disobeying her father's command in her birth home, chooses a Parbate Brahmin youth as her own husband; contrary to the social tradition whereby in the marital home one must bear children only through intercourse with one's husband, she conceives by another man and bears a daughter; and when compelled to choose between husband and daughter, giving precedence to motherhood, she sets forth a consciousness of resistance — that women can sustain their lives even without a husband's support. Her revolt against patriarchy demonstrates that conscious women, contending against gender discrimination, are capable of keeping hold of their dreams.
australian_english: Through Indramaya, Bishweshwar Prasad Koirala's novel Teen Ghumti lays out the oppression and discrimination of patriarchy as it runs through Nepali society. Feudal culture seems to have shaped the development of Nepali society over the ages. Feudalism seems to hang over the family in a feudal society. In Nepali society, men are found to hold sway. In a feudal society, the father's role within the family seems to be there. In Nepali society too, the father's role within the family seems to be the main one. The idea that sons are seen as entitled to the father's property still seems to hold up even today. Women's role in society doesn't seem to be independent, because until a woman gets married she has to live under her father's watch; likewise, after marriage she has to live under her husband's orders, and in old age she has to live under her son's say — so they seem to be stuck with men from birth through to death. Against the way Nepali society acts, as though women don't want freedom, Indramaya — going against her father's word in her birth home — picks a Parbate Brahmin boy as her own husband; against the social tradition that in the marital home she should only have children through intercourse with her husband, she falls pregnant to another man and gives birth to a girl; and when it comes to choosing between her husband and her daughter, she puts motherhood first and puts forward a resistant consciousness that women can get by even without a husband's support. Her revolt against patriarchy shows that switched-on women, fighting gender discrimination, can hang on to their dreams.
informal_english: So Bishweshwar Prasad Koirala's novel Teen Ghumti gets at how patriarchy oppresses and discriminates against people in Nepali society, told through Indramaya. Feudal values have basically been shaping Nepali society for ages. Feudalism's influence shows up in the feudal family too. Men call the shots in Nepali society. In a feudal family, the dad's the boss. Same in Nepali society — the dad's role in the family is the big one. Sons are still seen as the ones who get the father's property, and that's still going strong today. Women don't get to be independent, because before marriage you have to live under your dad's care, after marriage you have to do what your husband says, and in old age you have to live under your son — bottom line, women are stuck under men from birth to death. Against the whole Nepali way of acting like women don't want freedom, Indramaya goes against her dad's orders at her birth home and picks a Parbate Brahmin boy as her own husband; against the tradition that in her marital home she should have kids only with her husband, she gets pregnant by another man and has a daughter; and when it comes down to choosing between her husband and her daughter, she puts motherhood first and shows a defiant consciousness that women can make it on their own without a husband's support. Her revolt against patriarchy shows that switched-on women fighting gender discrimination can hang on to their dreams.
